name: Must I File 2026
purpose: Decides whether a US taxpayer must file a federal income tax return for tax year 2026. Send filing status, filers 65 or older, gross income, and three yes or no answers; it answers file, refund, none or review, and invalid for anything else.
inputLabel: status seniors gross dependent special payments

promise.headline: Says file exactly when 2026 federal rules require a return.
promise.detail: Gross income is compared with the 2026 threshold for your filing status and age, after dependents, self-employment and special taxes are checked first.

claim: INV-001 to INV-006: dependents always get review; special items and withheld tax never get none; single above $18,150 and joint above $35,500 always get file; no income and no special items never get file.

proposition.name: judge
proposition.text:
judge request :=
  if dependent = yes then review
  else if special = yes then file
  else if threshold status seniors <= gross then file
  else if payments = yes then refund
  else none

threshold: separate 5; single 16100 or 18150 at 65; head 24150 or 26200 at 65; joint 32200, 33850 with one 65, 35500 with two
proposition.plain: A dependent is sent to review. Self-employment of $400 or more, advance premium credits, HSA distributions or special taxes mean you must file. Otherwise you must file when gross income reaches the 2026 threshold for your status and age. Below it, filing gets withheld tax or refundable credits back.
